ethics-search.note: Searched by first and last name for every candidate; no record means none in EFDMS.

promises.value: Continue to make developers pay their fair share.
promises.note: Campaign site is undated; listed by Ballotpedia for the 2024 race.

promises.value: Fight to keep taxes low, budgets balanced, and county spending transparent.
Work with the Sheriff to keep families safe and fund new initiatives to reduce violent crimes.
Focus on keeping housing affordable, especially in urban cores.
Develop new programs and projects that protect the quantity and quality of drinking water.

In his 2022 race he highlighted opposing a brownfield designation for the former Pebble Creek Country Club, objecting to a yard waste incinerator zoning change in Lutz, backing a New Tampa Performing Arts Center and seeking funds for residential road paving.
Proposed adding $250,000 to the county budget to speed a potential Kinnan Street connection to Mansfield Boulevard (reported during his 2018 District 2 campaign).

electionHistory.note: County page says first elected in 2002. Official 2002 results are not on the SOE results archive, so vote share is not available.

electionHistory.result: Kept seat; no District 2 contest appears in the official 2006 primary or general results
electionHistory.note: Neighborhood News (nno-hagan-2018) reports he held District 2 from 2002 to 2010. The SOE results do not say whether he was unopposed.
Linda Saul-Sena (DEM) 42.49% (131,504); Jim Hosler (NPA) 4.83% (14,957). No District 5 contest in the 2010 primary results (soe-2010p).

electionHistory.result: Re-elected; no District 5 contest appears in the 2014 primary or general results
electionHistory.note: Osprey Observer (Dec 17, 2014) calls him re-elected for Countywide District 5. SOE ENR pages soe-2014p and soe-2014g list no District 5 race.

keyPositions.value: Voted yes on the Development and Funding Agreement, Guaranty and Team Non-Relocation Agreement for a Rays ballpark (RCS 5622; passed 5 to 2).
Before the Rays vote he said: "To be a world-class community requires vision, courage, bold leadership, and the ability to think big."
Voted yes on the non-binding Rays memorandum of understanding (RCS 5486).
Voted no on a motion to approve the finalized ZooTampa public-private partnership and proceed to a contract (RCS 5654; Cohen, Hagan and Myers voted no).
Voted yes to adopt FY2027 millage rates (RCS 5671).
Voted no on enacting the ordinance setting the Community Investment Tax renewal referendum (RCS 4308, Ordinance 24-3; Hagan and Kemp voted no).
Voted no on approving the School Board's Nov 5, 2024 referendum for additional operating property taxes (RCS 4437; 3 yes, 4 no).
Voted no on placing the 1 percent transportation surtax ordinance on the Nov 8, 2022 ballot (RCS 3284, Ordinance 22-9).
Voted no on the resolution calling the Aug 23, 2022 School Board referendum (RCS 3299).
Only no vote on transmitting an Urban Service Area expansion of about 295.6 acres on Lutz Lake Fern Road (RCS 4886).
Voted yes to adopt FY2026 millage and budget (RCS 5124, 5125; unanimous).
Roll-call tally (Glass Ballot count of the Clerk PDF, Yes/No/not voting): 2023 476/14/22; 2024 409/17/20; 2025 491/17/37; 2026 through Sep 24: 384/11/13.
County page calls him the board's leading voice for a Rays ballpark in Ybor City and credits him with creating the Tampa/Hillsborough Film Commission.
Campaign site claims he "voted 20 times to lower property taxes" and "voted to impose term limits on county politicians" (not checked against roll calls).
PolitiFact rated Mostly False his Dec 2013 claim that studies suggest the 2017 College Football Playoff championship game would bring about 1,700 to 1,800 full-time jobs.

financialDisclosures.note: Not in EFDMS; earlier forms must be requested from the Commission on Ethics.

conflicts.value: Ethics complaint 14-124 resolved by stipulation (final order 14-117) on Article II, Section 8 of the Florida Constitution (financial disclosure).
Florida Politics reports the 2014 complaint led Hagan to pay a $2,000 fine for failing to properly disclose assets on financial disclosure forms.

Aug 2014: the Commission on Ethics agreed to investigate a complaint by George Niemann that Hagan's disclosure listed an investment account ($401,000) and retirement accounts ($219,000) without naming specific assets. Hagan called the complaint "laughable".

A complaint by Niemann and three others alleging free campaign help from consultant Beth Leytham in connection with a Go Hillsborough contract was dismissed by the Commission on Ethics; the Sheriff's Office found no criminal violations in 2016 (as reported).
Hagan's petition to recover attorney fees from complainant (F 15-215, final order 18-014) was dismissed.
No Abstain votes recorded for Hagan in the 2018 to 2026 Clerk vote comparisons.

promises.value: On the voter-approved transportation sales tax: "If I'm elected and it's overturned, I absolutely will vote to put it back on the ballot."
Said of the 2018 transportation tax: "I supported it when it was on the ballot. I support it now."
Said he would bring his Tampa City Council work on stormwater and flooding to District 1 (reporter's paraphrase).

electionHistory.note: Julie Jenkins 28.94% (4,199); Tony DeSisto 12.33%; Dennis Meyers 7.68%; Joseph V. Citro 6.74%.
Jane Castor 48.0% and David Straz 15.5% advanced to the runoff.
